subject: Dedicated GPU pool surge causing elevated latency and 5xx — requesting exec standup
messages:
From: MonetaryAI SRE <ops@monetaryai.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: High latency + 5xx spikes on our dedicated pool (critical)

Ben —

We started seeing sustained token-latency increases starting ~08:40 PDT and are observing a ~12% rate of 5xx for requests routed to our reserved pool (pool-id: rsv-1223). Tail latency is up to 1.2s/token (normally ~0.08s/token) and our queues are building. This is materially impacting inference throughput for our two highest-volume endpoints.

We've attached a short metrics export and a sample trace (svc-metrics-09-12-2027.csv). Please escalate — monetaryai is on a full-production SLA.

What we need: immediate mitigation (fallback or temporary capacity), and an ETA to restore normal latency.

—Amit (SRE)

Attachment: svc-metrics-09-12-2027.csv (metrics CSV, 120k rows)
Attachment: brief-log-snippet.txt (log excerpt)

Date: Mon, 2 May 2027 09:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High latency + 5xx spikes on our dedicated pool (critical)

Amit — thanks for the data and the quick heads up. We're on this. Quick plan in flight: 

1) Irene's SRE team will run a headroom check and temporarily divert low-risk traffic to a hosted fallback model (same architecture, lower perf SLAs) to reduce pressure on rsv-1223.
2) We'll open an emergency capacity window (burst) while we investigate root cause (kernel/queueing/other tenants).
3) Naomi will coordinate customer comms and track any SLA credit implications.

Irene — please confirm whether we can toggle the hosted fallback for MonetaryAI now and whether the burst window needs leadership approval. Vivek — assigning for visibility and quick approval if cost >$2k/hr.

Ben

Ben / Amit —

We validated rsv-1223 headroom at 09:30 PDT: all GPUs in the pool are at 95–100% utilization and the request queue is climbing. Early signal shows elevated KV cache churn plus a high ratio of long-sequence requests (seq_len > 2048) that are increasing per-token work.

Immediate mitigations we can apply in the next 10–20 minutes:
- Enable hosted fallback (route 20% of MonetaryAI production traffic to hosted-variant to relieve queueing).
- Temporarily lower batch size for the reserved pool from 16 -> 8 for MonetaryAI routes (reduces tail latency at cost of throughput efficiency).
- Enable aggressive prefix cache (keep recent prefixes pinned for 30m for this customer).

I can flip the hosted fallback and batch size now. For the burst capacity (spin additional reserved nodes) we need leadership approval: estimated incremental cost $1,800/hr to bridge the next 2–4 hours. Naomi, Vivek — can you confirm?

Irene

- 09:45 PDT: Reduced batch size from 16 -> 8 for MonetaryAI on reserved pool; tail latency improved ~40% on sampled requests.
- 09:50 PDT: Spun emergency burst capacity (3 additional reserved nodes) under approved $2k/hr window; utilization returned to 60–70% after shift.

- Short term: Keep hosted fallback and reduced batch size for 2 hours, then re-evaluate.
- Customer comms: Naomi sent a customer note offering an SLA credit if degradation >60m (she will follow up).
- Billing/finance: Sergio will flag spend to finance and track actual burst cost to DEAL-48721.
